title: Comparison of efficacy and safety of combined phacoemulsification, goniosynechialysis and goniotomy with trabeculectomy in advanced primary angle-closure glaucoma: a retrospective observational study

license.statement: CC BY (article <license>: 'Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY)'; no version number or licence URL given in the XML)

indication: medically uncontrolled advanced primary angle-closure glaucoma (MD < -12 dB) with 360-degree peripheral anterior synechiae and visually significant cataract, age >= 40 years; 4 of 30 trabeculectomy eyes had previous surgery; retrospective observational single-center study (China)

groups.description: trabeculectomy with mitomycin C (0.4 mg/ml, 2.5 min), scleral flap with adjustable sutures and peripheral iridectomy (the study's comparator / control group); 30 eyes of 29 patients (T1!R2C3)

exclusions.what: PEI + GSL + GT group IOP series (Table 2 rows R1-R5; Table 3 column C2)
exclusions.reason: follow-up means are Last-Observation-Carried-Forward imputed (Results: 43 eyes declined to 20 at 12 months, LOCF used for the missing eyes, including eyes that underwent other surgeries for poor efficacy or complications), so the tabulated values at each time are not in vivo IOP measured at that time (protocol inclusion 1) and are censored at additional surgery with imputation (brief: censored analysis sets excluded); this arm was declared the treatment group (role would have been 'treated', procedure 'angle_mims')

exclusions.what: Table 2 t and P value rows; Table 3 t and P value columns
exclusions.reason: test statistics and p-values are not admissible
medians and medication counts are not admissible IOP series; noted only

exclusions.what: Table 7 complete and qualified success rates; Figures 2-3 Kaplan-Meier
exclusions.reason: success proportions / Kaplan-Meier estimates are not admissible

exclusions.what: Table 5 visual field MD and Table 6 complications

notes: Reference kind 'preoperative_medicated': inclusion required IOP > 21 mmHg with the maximum-dose use of IOP-lowering medications; preoperative glaucoma medications are tabulated as medians (Table 1 R11, Table 4 R2); no washout described.
Tonometer not stated in the article, so method 'unstated'.
Day 1 and Day 7 converted as 1/30.4375 and 7/30.4375 months (rounded to 4 decimals).
The abstract states that each patient completed a 12-month follow-up, while the Results report losses to follow-up in the PEI + GSL + GT group only.

Role of the trabeculectomy group is 'control' because the authors designate PEI + GSL + GT as the treatment group and trabeculectomy (the 'gold standard') as the control group in the sample-size calculation.

series.baseline_label: Table 2 TRAB block, column 'Baseline (n = 30)', row 'IOP (mm Hg)' (same cell text as Table 1 'Baseline IOP (mm Hg)', T1!R4C3, and Table 3 'Preoperative')
series.notes: mean ± SD (Methods); columns Baseline, Day 1, Day 7, Month 1, 3, 6, 9, 12; eyes 30 at baseline and 29 at every postoperative column (T2!R7 and the Day headers in T2!R6); the reason for the missing eye is not stated (Table 6 / text: one trabeculectomy eye developed malignant glaucoma requiring secondary surgery), and the article does not describe an outcome-defined exclusion or imputation for this group; Table 3 repeats the same means
